target.title: fix: tighten readSchema.limit from Type.Number to Type.Integer
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `readSchema.limit` accepts floating-point values via `Type.Number()` while the sibling field `offset` already correctly uses `Type.Integer({ minimum: 1 })`. This inconsistency means an LLM can pass `limit=10.5` and get 10 lines back instead of the expected 10-11.

**Solution**: Tighten `limit` to `Type.Integer()` — matching the same schema's `offset` field. TypeBox rejects float values at the parameter parsing stage, before reaching runtime.

**What changed / NOT changed**: One type annotation changed in `src/agents/sessions/tools/read.ts`. Runtime behavior is identical — `normalizePositiveLimit` already applies `Math.floor` to the value. No config, CLI, or public API surface changed. No dependencies added or updated. This is a consistency fix to align `limit` with the already-correct `offset` field in the same schema.

**merge-risk declaration**: No — schema-only change to an internal tool schema type. No session state, auth, message delivery, or security boundary involved.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Schema-level validation tightening — reject float values for `readSchema.limit` at the TypeBox parameter parsing stage. The field represents a line count which is inherently an integer value.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64 (local workstation)

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` (exit 0), `pnpm test vitest.agents-tools.config.ts` (54 passed)

**After-fix evidence**: Build and test output confirm the change compiles and does not regress existing behavior. The runtime behavior is unchanged — consumers already use `Math.floor` via `normalizePositiveLimit` — so no before/after behavioral diff exists.

**Observed result after the fix**: N/A (schema-only, no behavioral change)

**What was not tested**: End-to-end LLM read tool invocation with float limit values. The schema change is validated at the TypeBox layer and does not alter runtime execution paths.

## Tests and validation

target.title: fix(macos): fit onboarding window on short screens
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #98674.

The macOS onboarding window used a fixed preferred content height and `window.center()`, so on short visible desktop areas the first-run window could extend below the screen and hide the bottom setup/navigation action.

## Why This Change Was Made

This routes onboarding window placement through the existing `WindowPlacement.centeredFrame` helper so the actual NSWindow frame is clamped to the active screen visible frame before display. The SwiftUI root view now allows its height to shrink between the onboarding minimum and preferred height, so the clamped window can adapt instead of insisting on the full preferred height.

## User Impact

Users on shorter displays or desktops with reduced visible height should be able to see and click the onboarding bottom actions instead of getting stuck during first-run setup.

## Evidence

- Added `WindowPlacementTests` coverage for onboarding frame clamping on a 690pt short visible frame and for preserving preferred height on tall screens.

target.title: fix(mattermost): bound websocket handshake waits at 30s
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mattermost's default websocket factory set `maxPayload` but not `handshakeTimeout`. `createMattermostConnectOnce` waits for the `open` event; when a peer accepts TCP but never completes the websocket upgrade, that wait never ends. Slack relay and browser CDP already bound handshake waits at 30s.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass `handshakeTimeout: MATTERMOST_WEBSOCKET_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS` (30_000) in the default Mattermost `WebSocket` options, matching Slack relay.

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A Mattermost host that accepted TCP without completing the websocket handshake could pin the channel reconnect loop forever on that attempt.

**After:** Handshake waits fail closed after 30s (`WebSocketClosedBeforeOpenError` / close before open), allowing the reconnect loop to continue.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-websocket.ts`
- Production caller under test: `createMattermostConnectOnce` with a real `ws` client against a local TCP server that never completes the upgrade

target.title: fix: avoid false restart failure during startup migrations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators updating or restarting OpenClaw could receive a readiness failure after about 60 seconds even though the gateway was still healthy and completing a legitimate startup migration. Observed migrations can take substantially longer, causing the update path to report failure while the gateway becomes ready shortly afterward.

## Why This Change Was Made

The managed restart readiness owner now recognizes the canonical startup-migration lease and grants a bounded migration-aware wait, followed by the existing readiness window once migration work finishes. Normal startup failures still fail promptly, and non-migration restarts retain the existing timeout. The update subprocess also receives the update step's configured timeout so its outer watchdog cannot terminate a valid extended wait early.

## User Impact

Updates and managed restarts no longer report a false failure while a healthy startup migration is actively progressing. Crashes, stopped processes, stale leases, plugin/channel/version mismatches, and ordinary readiness timeouts retain their existing failure behavior.

## Evidence

- Added focused coverage for a healthy long migration and genuine readiness failures/timeouts.
- Focused Vitest proof: 333 tests passed across daemon service merging, the startup migration checkpoint, restart-health, daemon lifecycle, update command, and full update CLI suites.
- Targeted Oxfmt and Oxlint checks passed; `git diff --check` is clean.
- Fresh autoreview after CI/review fixes reported no accepted/actionable findings (`patch is correct`, confidence 0.92).
- Blacksmith Testbox and AWS Crabbox were unavailable in this environment because the required organization/cloud credentials were not present; CI remains the remote Linux proof.

target.title: fix(cli): reject noncanonical trajectory export requests
target.body:
## Summary

Reject non-canonical base64url values passed to `sessions export-trajectory --request-json-base64`.

## What Problem This Solves

The command checked only the base64url alphabet before sending the value to Node's permissive decoder. A valid-alphabet suffix that makes the encoded length one modulo four was silently discarded, so malformed CLI input was interpreted as a valid trajectory-export request.

## User Impact

Operators receive an explicit encoded-request error at the parser boundary instead of a misleading later session lookup result for malformed input.

## Origin / follow-up

Follows #72936.

Gap this fills: #72936 introduced the encoded trajectory-export request path, but its parser accepted a non-canonical base64url representation.

Consistency: this keeps validation with the command's request decoder, matching the repository's decode-and-reencode strictness pattern.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

Fresh GitHub search found no substantive open PR or issue for strict decoding of `request-json-base64` / `Encoded trajectory export request`. Open #104708 is a separate `/export-session` filesystem authorization change and has no parser or file overlap.

## Merge risk

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Malformed CLI request input currently appears to select a missing session rather than being rejected as malformed.
- **Risk labels considered:** compatibility.
- **Risk explanation:** Non-canonical values that Node previously normalized by discarding a suffix now fail at the documented encoded-request boundary.
- **Why acceptable:** The command producer emits canonical base64url, and canonical input retains its existing session-lookup behavior.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High; the fix is a two-file parser regression guard with current-main RED evidence, a real CLI after-fix proof, and a canonical control.
- **Patch quality notes:** Root-cause validation only; no fallback, default, retry, or unrelated cleanup was added.
- **Target test file:** `src/commands/export-trajectory.test.ts`.
- **Root cause:** Alphabet validation alone does not make Node's base64url decode exact; `Buffer.from` accepts and truncates a length-one-modulo-four suffix.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** Decode once, then require its canonical base64url re-encoding to equal the supplied request before JSON parsing or session lookup.
- **What did NOT change:** Session resolution, trajectory export, approval behavior, output schema, and provider/channel behavior.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The guard is in the canonical CLI request parser before it creates the resolved options consumed by session lookup; it does not affect persisted session or trajectory data.
- **Scenario locked in:** `eyJzZXNzaW9uS2V5IjoieCJ9A` contains the canonical request plus a valid-alphabet suffix and must be rejected before session lookup.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The equality check covers the decoder's silent normalization in one place while retaining the existing alphabet and maximum-length limits.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A malformed encoded trajectory-export request is rejected at the CLI parser boundary instead of being treated as a valid session request.
- **Canonical reachability path:** CLI input → Commander parses `--request-json-base64` unchanged → `decodeExportTrajectoryRequest` validates and normalizes the base64url request → `exportTrajectoryCommand` would perform session lookup → CLI reports the result to the user.
- **Boundary crossed:** no external boundary; the proof invokes the real local OpenClaw CLI entry and crosses its argument parser into the production command runtime.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Searched `packages/media-core/src/base64.ts` (standard base64 only, not this base64url CLI contract) and `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/bootstrap.ts` (existing decode-and-reencode strictness pattern). The guard stays in this command's canonical owner; no provider constraint applies.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux with Node v22.22.0, using `node --import tsx src/entry.ts` from the final OpenClaw worktree.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx src/entry.ts sessions export-trajectory --request-json-base64 eyJzZXNzaW9uS2V5IjoieCJ9A --json`, followed by the same command with canonical `eyJzZXNzaW9uS2V5IjoieCJ9`.
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
CASE=malformed-after-fix
EXIT=1
OUTPUT=Failed to decode trajectory export request: Encoded trajectory export request is invalid
CASE=canonical-control
EXIT=1
OUTPUT=Session not found: x. Run openclaw sessions to see available sessions.
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The malformed request stops before session lookup; canonical input retains the existing missing-session result.
- **What was not tested:** A full repository `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit --pretty false` could not complete in this environment because TypeScript exhausted both its default 4 GiB heap and a 6 GiB retry. No external provider or channel is involved in this CLI-only path.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

## Review findings addressed

No prior review findings; this is a new focused PR.

## Regression Test Plan

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/commands/export-trajectory.test.ts` — 10 tests passed, including the non-canonical request regression.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/commands/export-trajectory.ts src/commands/export-trajectory.test.ts` — passed.
- The real CLI proof above covers malformed-after-fix and canonical-control behavior.

## Risk / Compatibility

Canonical base64url requests remain accepted. Only values that Node silently normalizes rather than decodes exactly now fail with the command's existing encoded-request error.

## What was not changed

This does not alter generated command syntax, session storage, trajectory artifacts, or any network/provider integration.

## Root Cause

`Buffer.from(value, "base64url")` is intentionally permissive. The previous implementation accepted any valid-alphabet string and treated the decoder output as authoritative, allowing a malformed suffix to disappear before JSON parsing.

target.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch
target.body:
Closes #103077.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an in-process plugin-runtime caller could use `sessions.patch` to archive, unarchive, or otherwise mutate a session owned by a different plugin. `sessions.delete` already rejects cross-plugin cleanup, but `sessions.patch` performed the mutation with no ownership check.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` helper in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` was generalized to `rejectPluginRuntimeSessionMismatch` so it can report the action (`delete` or `patch`) in its error message. `sessions.patch` now calls this helper both before acquiring the lifecycle mutation lock and again inside `applyPatch` under the lock, matching the double-check pattern used by `sessions.delete`.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:**
1. `sessions.patch` now propagates the authenticated plugin owner into newly created session rows, so a plugin-created row remains mutable by its creator on subsequent patches.
2. Plugin-runtime callers now fail closed on legacy ownerless rows. Rows created before plugin ownership existed have no safe plugin authority, so they are rejected rather than allowing arbitrary plugin adoption.

## User Impact

Plugin-runtime callers can no longer patch sessions created by other plugins. Their own sessions continue to work unchanged, including sessions they create through `sessions.patch`. Legacy ownerless sessions are no longer mutable by plugin-runtime callers; operators or non-plugin clients can still manage them.

## Evidence

- Added regression test `sessions.patch limits plugin-runtime mutations to sessions owned by that plugin` in `src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts`. It verifies that a `memory-core` plugin-runtime client is rejected when archiving/unarchiving sessions owned by `other-plugin`, while patching a `memory-core`-owned session still succeeds.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch rejects plugin-runtime patches on legacy ownerless sessions` to enforce the fail-closed upgrade boundary.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch stamps pluginOwnerId when patch creates a new session` to prove owner propagation on creation.
- Added unit coverage in `src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` for `pluginOwnerId` stamping behavior.
- Focused local run:
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` → 260 passed across gateway-core/gateway-server/gateway-client/gateway-methods shards.
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts` → new ownership tests pass (one pre-existing unrelated failure caused by local `git` binary not supporting `git init -b main`).
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

The focused tests run against a loopback Gateway server harness (`startGatewayServerHarness`), so the foreign-rejection and owner-success behavior is verified through real in-process plugin-runtime gateway wiring. This environment does not have the `crabbox` binary, so a redacted terminal log from a live deployed gateway cannot be generated locally.

target.body:
Closes #105532

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users editing configuration in the Control UI could keep changing structured, raw, or Quick Settings controls while a save, apply, reload, or update operation was pending. The subsequent authoritative refresh then replaced those accepted edits without warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

Configuration operations now publish their pending state before the first asynchronous wait, and every config-backed editor uses one operation-wide busy state. Update-triggered locking follows the existing restart reconciliation lifecycle through managed-service handoff and reconnect instead of ending when the initial RPC returns.

## User Impact

Configuration controls now lock for the full duration of an operation and become editable again only after the authoritative result settles. Users can no longer type changes into a draft window that is about to be replaced by a save, reload, apply, or Gateway update refresh.

## Evidence

- Before fix, a real-Gateway Playwright run observed the raw editor enabled during delayed `config.set`; late input was accepted and then absent after settlement.
- After fix, the rebuilt Control UI reported the editor disabled during the same delayed request, rejected the late fill, retained no late marker, and restored the original configuration.

Fixes an issue where users discovering OpenClaw gateways over a tailnet could miss wide-area Bonjour gateways when the Tailscale CLI printed diagnostic text around its JSON status output.

target.title: fix(scripts): bound conflict-marker scan reads to prevent OOM on large files
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`pnpm check:no-conflict-markers` reads every candidate tracked file returned by `git grep` into memory whole via `fs.readFileSync`. A single large generated or text file that slips through the binary heuristic can exhaust the process memory before the scan completes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Cap each scanned file at `MAX_CONFLICT_MARKER_SCAN_BYTES` (50 MiB).
- Files larger than the cap are skipped with a warning instead of being read into memory.
- The cap is applied before the read, so the oversized content is never buffered.
- The limit is injectable for testing; the production default remains 50 MiB.

## User Impact

- Normal conflict-marker checks on source and documentation files are unchanged.
- Oversized files fail open (skipped with a warning) rather than risking an OOM crash.
- CI and pre-commit runs remain robust against accidental large-file commits.

## Evidence

Local focused test passes:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts --run
```

Result:

```
✓ |tooling| test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts (5 tests) 98ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  5 passed (5)
```

Added regression test asserting oversized files are skipped while smaller files with markers are still detected.

Real behavior proof:

```bash
node -e "
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const { findConflictMarkersInFiles } = require('./scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs');
const tmpFile = path.join(require('os').tmpdir(), 'large-conflict-marker-test.txt');
fs.writeFileSync(tmpFile, 'a'.repeat(60 * 1024 * 1024));
let readCount = 0;
const readFile = (p) => { readCount++; return fs.readFileSync(p); };
const warnings = [];
findConflictMarkersInFiles([tmpFile], readFile, fs.statSync, (m) => warnings.push(m));
console.log('violations:', 0);
console.log('readCount:', readCount);
console.log('warnings:', warnings);
fs.unlinkSync(tmpFile);
"
```

Output:

```
violations: 0
readCount: 0
warnings: [
  '[check-no-conflict-markers] skipping oversized file: /tmp/large-conflict-marker-test.txt (62914560 bytes)'
]
```

Also verified:

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts` — clean
- `git diff --check` — clean

target.title: feat(memory-wiki): add wiki_open_items tool to list unresolved questions and contradictions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`memory-wiki` already detects unresolved knowledge-health items — open questions, page/claim contradictions, and low-confidence pages/claims — but they are only reachable as side effects: rendered into the compiled `reports/*.md` dashboards or surfaced inline by `wiki_lint`'s structural pass. There is no first-class, machine-readable way for an agent (or a future maintenance flow) to *enumerate* just the open items, with their text and page location, so they can be worked through one at a time.

## Why does it matter / user impact?

Agents that want to help a user resolve accumulated wiki debt (answer open questions, reconcile contradictions, re-confirm low-confidence claims) currently have to scrape a human-oriented dashboard or re-run a broad lint and parse its prose. This adds a small, read-only `wiki_open_items` tool that returns a structured list of exactly those items, filterable by kind and limit. It is the enabling primitive for interactive "work through the open items" resolution flows (see #105494) without committing the project to any particular UX for that yet.

## Why in core (extensions/) rather than a third-party plugin?

Per CONTRIBUTING, most features should be third-party plugins. This one is deliberately *not*: it is a thin read-only accessor over `memory-wiki`'s own already-internal derivations (`readQueryableWikiPages`, the contradiction-cluster builders, and `collectWikiClaimHealth`). A third-party plugin could not reach those without either the `unsafe-local` private-path escape hatch or duplicating the parsing/derivation logic — both of which would be strictly worse than exposing one more tool from the plugin that already owns this data. It registers no new config, no new dependencies, and no new surface beyond a single tool that mirrors the existing `wiki_lint` shape.

## Evidence

Change set (7 files, +321/-9):
- `src/open-items.ts` (new) — pure `deriveMemoryWikiOpenItems(pages)` + disk `collectMemoryWikiOpenItems(rootDir)`; enumerates 5 kinds (open-question, page-contradiction, claim-contradiction, low-confidence-page, low-confidence-claim).
- `src/open-items.test.ts` (new) — 3 cases (all kinds; cross-page claim-contradiction cluster; clean vault → empty).
- `src/tool.ts` — `createWikiOpenItemsTool` with `kinds`/`limit` filters, mirroring `wiki_lint`.
- `index.ts` — registers `wiki_open_items`.
- `index.test.ts` — tool-registry assertions updated.
- `openclaw.plugin.json` — declares `wiki_open_items` in `contracts.tools`.
- `docs/plugins/memory-wiki.md` — documents the new agent tool.

Validation (all run in a clean Cloudflare crabbox container against `upstream/main`):
- `pnpm build` ✓
- `tsgo:extensions` + `tsgo:extensions:test` ✓
- `oxlint` 0 errors / 0 warnings ✓
- `oxfmt --check` ✓
- `test:extension memory-wiki` → **307/307** ✓
- `test:contracts:plugins` → **986/986** (43 files, incl. the plugin-registration contract lane that enforces the manifest tool contract) ✓
- `format:docs:check` + markdownlint → clean ✓

### Real behavior proof

`collectMemoryWikiOpenItems` run against a seeded vault returns the expected structured items:

```
$ node -e '... collectMemoryWikiOpenItems(vault) ...'
[
  { kind: "open-question", page: "topics/routing.md", text: "Is the gateway bound to 0.0.0.0 intentionally?" },
  { kind: "page-contradiction", page: "topics/routing.md", text: "conflicts with topics/network.md on bind address" },
  { kind: "claim-contradiction", page: "topics/network.md", text: "\"LAN is open\" vs \"LAN is firewalled\"" },
  { kind: "low-confidence-claim", page: "topics/network.md", text: "gateway bind is temporary (confidence 0.3)" }
]
```

Filtering (`kinds: ["open-question"]`, `limit: 1`) narrows the result as expected; a clean vault returns `[]`.

## AI assistance disclosure

This PR was authored with assistance from Claude Code (Claude Opus 4.8). A local `codex review --base origin/main` was run; it flagged one P1 (the tool was registered in `index.ts` but missing from `openclaw.plugin.json` `contracts.tools`, which the plugin registry and contract test enforce), which is fixed in this branch. The re-review returned clean.

target.title: feat(ui): collapse completed turn work behind a "Worked for X" rollup
target.body:
Closes #105010

## What Problem This Solves

After an agent run finishes, the Control UI chat thread keeps every intermediate step of the turn — tool activity groups and running commentary — at full height. Long runs bury the final answer, and the thread never says how long the run took or gives an at-a-glance done signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Once a turn reaches terminal state, its intermediate work (tool groups plus assistant commentary ahead of the final reply) now collapses behind one slim disclosure row — a check icon, "Worked for 2m 52s", and a chevron — so completed turns read final-output-first while the details stay one click away. Live turns never collapse (in-flight stream runs and, while the run works, the trailing or reply-less turn stay expanded), so the collapse itself doubles as the done indicator. Turns whose tools errored without a recovering reply default to expanded with the existing error styling so failures stay visible. Web Control UI only; the collapse is a render-time pass over the existing chat item pipeline and reuses the activity-group disclosure pattern and per-session expansion store.

## User Impact

Completed turns in Control UI chat show the user message, one "Worked for X" rollup, and the final reply — both in history and the moment a live run finishes. Clicking the rollup expands the full intermediate detail; clicking again re-collapses it. Runs that ended without a reply (aborted, or tool errors) collapse too once the session is idle, with error turns surfacing expanded.

## Evidence

- Focused suite on Blacksmith Testbox: `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread.test.ts` — 86/86 passed (8 new `collapseCompletedTurnWork` tests: collapse shape, duration, live-turn guards, reply-less turns, error flagging, divider boundaries, per-turn independence). Fixes an issue where ordinary agent turns could fail during secrets runtime preparation when a disabled or non-selected web-search provider had an unresolved `SecretRef` configured.

target.title: fix(memory): bound unsignaled remote HTTP with default timeoutMs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory remote HTTP (`withRemoteHttpResponse`) only forwarded an optional caller `AbortSignal`. Embedding batch / `postJson` callers often omit a signal (Google/OpenAI/Voyage upload and status polls), so a peer that accepts TCP but never returns headers could hang the Gateway forever. Idle body caps never start until headers arrive.

## Why This Change Was Made

When callers omit `signal`, install a shared hang floor via existing `fetchWithSsrFGuard` `timeoutMs`:

- Default: `MEMORY_REMOTE_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` = 120s (aligned with memory remote batch budgets so large uploads are not clamped below established policy)
- Explicit `timeoutMs` override still wins
- Callers that already pass `AbortSignal` keep their own deadline (no default floor)

Also forward optional `timeoutMs` through `postJson` so production JSON POST callers can override the floor without reimplementing the wrapper.

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** Unsignaled memory remote HTTP (embedding batch upload/status, shared `postJson`) could hang indefinitely on a stalled upstream.

**After:** Unsignaled requests fail closed after 120s (`TimeoutError` / `request timed out`). Callers with `AbortSignal` keep their budget.

target.title: fix(discord): retry reply session init conflicts to prevent silent message loss
target.body:
Closes #102381

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord inbound messages could be silently dropped when a reply session initialization conflict (`reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>`) raced with another turn finishing or another event initializing the same session. Telegram, Signal, and Slack already retry this transient condition; Discord did not, so the user saw no reply and the message was lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added bounded exponential backoff retry inside `processDiscordMessageInner` (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts`) to match the existing Telegram callback-submit pattern and Slack/Signal retry semantics. The retry only applies to the specific reply-session-init-conflict error string; all other errors fail fast on the first attempt. If the run is aborted while retrying, the loop stops cleanly and returns without throwing.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:** the retry boundary was narrowed so context/history preparation runs exactly once and only the dispatch/session-init attempt is retried. This prevents a Discord room event from being recorded twice when a conflict happens.

## User Impact

Discord users are far less likely to see a missing reply after sending a message that races with a session teardown or concurrent turn. Operators no longer need to ask the user to re-send; the retry covers the brief window where the session store CAS conflict occurs.

## Evidence

- Added a focused regression test suite in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts`:
  - retries with exponential backoff until dispatch succeeds (250 ms, 1000 ms, 2500 ms)
  - throws the last error after exhausting retries
  - does not retry unrelated dispatch errors
  - stops retrying when the abort signal fires
  - **records room event history exactly once across conflict retries** (new regression test for the narrowed boundary)
- Full local focused run:
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 120 passed
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 22 passed
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.abort-skip.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 198 passed
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

This environment does not have the `crabbox` binary or a live Discord bot token, so a redacted live Discord conflict-to-success trace cannot be generated locally. Requesting maintainer help to run the Discord live transport / QA Lab proof on Crabbox, or a maintainer can trigger `@clawsweeper re-review` if the current in-process test evidence is sufficient.

target.title: fix(feishu): pass timeoutMs through app-registration guarded fetch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Feishu app-registration HTTP went through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without a top-level `timeoutMs`. Sibling Feishu surfaces (`streaming-card`) already pass `timeoutMs` so undici dispatcher + guarded abort both fire. Registration previously relied only on `AbortSignal.timeout` inside `RequestInit`, which does not configure the guarded-fetch dispatcher hang floor the same way.

A Feishu/Lark accounts peer that accepts TCP but never returns headers could stall onboarding / QR registration longer than intended, especially if `init.signal` is dropped on a future refactor.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wire `timeoutMs` into `fetchFeishuJson` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard`, matching the streaming-card pattern:

- Default floor: existing `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` (10s) — keeps the tighter wizard budget (not the 30s `FEISHU_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` API client default)
- Optional `timeoutMs` on registration fetch options for tests / overrides
- Remove redundant `init.signal` timeouts now owned by the guarded fetch

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** Registration HTTP depended on `RequestInit.signal` alone; guarded-fetch `timeoutMs` / dispatcher hang floor was unset.

**After:** Every registration JSON call installs a 10s guarded `timeoutMs`. Hung accounts endpoints reject with `TimeoutError: request timed out`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where remote media downloads could drop the prefix of a `Content-Disposition: filename*=` filename when the header percent-encoded `/` or `\` inside the selected filename.

target.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in az login
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Interactive Microsoft Foundry onboarding uses `az login --use-device-code`. Before this PR, stdout/stderr stream errors on that child process could surface as unhandled stream failures or settle the login promise before the child process lifecycle was actually closed. On Windows, killing only the shell wrapper can also leave the shell-launched Azure CLI descendant alive.

## Why This Change Was Made

- add stdout/stderr `error` handlers for interactive `az login --use-device-code`
- move the stream-error shutdown path onto the public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/process-runtime` process-tree helpers instead of direct child-only `kill()` calls
- spawn `az login` with the SDK process-tree detach policy, so POSIX runs can signal the child process group and Windows shell launches can use the shared taskkill-backed process-tree path
- keep duplicate stream errors and late child `error` events idempotent: the first stream error wins and teardown runs once
- cover the lifecycle with mocked-timer regressions, a real spawned local `az` substitute process over real stdio pipes, and an SDK contract test for Windows taskkill routing

## User Impact

Users who hit a broken pipe or wrapper stream error during Microsoft Foundry `az login` should get one bounded login failure instead of a hung/stale login process, duplicate teardown, or a left-behind Windows Azure CLI descendant.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` — passed after commit `9f51c9e2bf`
- `node --import tsx scripts/check-no-extension-test-core-imports.ts` — passed after commit `9f51c9e2bf`; extension tests avoid direct core test/internal imports
- `node scripts/report-test-temp-creations.mjs --staged --json --fail-on-findings` — passed before commit `9f51c9e2bf`; output `[]`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.process.test.ts test/extension-test-boundary.test.ts` — passed after commit `9f51c9e2bf`; boundary shard 11 passed, microsoft-foundry shard 2 passed / 1 Windows-only skipped
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-sdk/process-runtime.test.ts extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.test.ts extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.process.test.ts test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` — passed after commit `d4d62c6fa6`; tooling shard 10 passed, plugin-sdk shard 1 passed, microsoft-foundry shard 6 passed / 1 Windows-only skipped
- Earlier mutation check: forcing the stream-error path to reject before child close made both real-process tests fail on the close-before-rejection assertions; reverting the mutation made the focused tests pass
- CI fixes addressed: `d4d62c6fa6` updated plugin SDK surface budgets for the three public process-tree helper exports; `9f51c9e2bf` keeps the extension process proof on public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/test-env` temp-dir helpers instead of repo-only test helper bridges or bare temp-dir exceptions

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Microsoft Foundry `az login --use-device-code` stdout/stderr stream errors are contained without an unhandled stream error, duplicate teardown, or settlement before the login process closes. The latest patch additionally prevents the stream-error cleanup from stopping only the Windows shell wrapper while leaving the shell-launched `az` descendant alive.

Real environment tested: local Linux Node source checkout. The proof uses a PATH-injected local `az` substitute executable — a real spawned process with real stdio pipes, not the Azure CLI and not an in-process mocked child.

Exact focused commands run after the latest patches:

```sh
node --import tsx scripts/check-no-extension-test-core-imports.ts
node scripts/report-test-temp-creations.mjs --staged --json --fail-on-findings
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.process.test.ts test/extension-test-boundary.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-sdk/process-runtime.test.ts extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.test.ts extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.process.test.ts test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts
```

Observed result after `9f51c9e2bf`: extension boundary script passed for 2404 extension files and 1 plugin helper; temp-dir report output `[]`; boundary shard 11 passed; microsoft-foundry shard 2 passed / 1 Windows-only skipped. Observed result after `d4d62c6fa6`: tooling shard 10 passed, plugin-sdk shard 1 passed, microsoft-foundry shard 6 passed / 1 Windows-only skipped.

The Linux real-process tests spy on `process.kill` and verify `SIGTERM` / `SIGKILL` are sent to the spawned process group (`-childPid`) through the SDK process-tree helper before the promise rejects. The SDK contract test mocks `process.platform === "win32"` and verifies `openclaw/plugin-sdk/process-runtime` routes `signalChildProcessTree` / `forceKillChildProcessTree` to `taskkill /T /PID <pid>` and `taskkill /F /T /PID <pid>` instead of calling `child.kill()`.

Windows-specific committed proof: `extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.process.test.ts` now contains a Windows-only real process test that launches a `.cmd` shell wrapper, records the descendant fake-az PID, forces a stdout stream error, and asserts the descendant exits before rejection. That test is intentionally `describe.skipIf(process.platform !== "win32")`; it was not run in this local Linux proof.

What was not tested: live Azure CLI/device-code authentication, a kernel-originated stdout read error, and the Windows-only `.cmd` descendant test on a native Windows host. Node offers no reliable local Linux way to force a kernel read error on `child.stdout`, so the runnable proof drives the real exported function with a real child process and forces the Node stream error on that real pipe.

Collision check: no open PR found for the Microsoft Foundry az login stream-error issue or `extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.ts`.

target.title: fix(acp): ACP session startup fails when backend does not advertise thinking config
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103802 — ACP sessions can fail at startup with:

```
AcpRuntimeError [ACP_BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED_CONTROL]: ACP session agent:opencode:acp:... does not advertise config option 'effort'. Supported config options: mode, model.
```

This happens when thinking is inherited from defaults/model profile and then applied to a backend that does not advertise a thinking config option.

## Why This Change Was Made

This patch fixes the ACPX capability-boundary regression by:

1. **Forward the getCapabilities input handle** — the manager-provided handle is now passed to the delegate so session-scoped configOptionKeys (including `reasoning_effort`) are visible.

2. **Advertise thinking aliases for Codex ACP only** — `thinking` and `thought_level` are injected as aliases when `reasoning_effort` is advertised, but only for Codex ACP sessions. The acpx `setConfigOption` only translates these aliases for Codex ACP, so advertising them to non-Codex agents would claim support that doesn't exist.

3. **Restore inherited thinking defaults** — the `resolveThinkingDefault` fallback is restored so configured/model-profile thinking still applies on backends that support it. The capability normalization (handle forwarding + alias advertising) already solves the rejection, so the defaults are safe to keep.

4. **Non-mutating alias injection** — delegate-owned capability arrays are cloned before modification.

## User Impact

- ACP sessions against limited backends (acpx, non-OC providers) no longer fail due to inherited default thinking values.
- Configured/model-profile thinking defaults still apply on backends that support them.
- Explicit `sessions_spawn(thinking: ...)` remains strict and fails visibly when unsupported.
- Non-Codex ACP agents are not advertised aliases that only the Codex-specific wrapper can translate.

## Evidence

### Before (main branch — broken)

`getCapabilities()` ignores the input handle entirely. The delegate receives no arguments, and no thinking aliases are injected:

```
$ git checkout main
$ npx vitest run extensions/acpx/src/repro-103958.test.ts --reporter=verbose

  [BEFORE - main] getCapabilities({handle}) → ["reasoning_effort","model"]
  [BEFORE - main] delegate called with: no arguments (input IGNORED)
  [BEFORE - main] thinking aliases: MISSING
  ❌ Gateway injects thinking default → backend REJECTS startup
```

### After (PR branch — fixed)

`getCapabilities(input)` forwards the handle to the delegate and injects `thinking` + `thought_level` aliases when `reasoning_effort` is advertised. Delegate-owned arrays are not mutated:

```
$ git checkout fix/acp-opencode-thinking-config
$ npx vitest run extensions/acpx/src/repro-103958.test.ts --reporter=verbose

  [AFTER - fix] getCapabilities(input) → ["reasoning_effort","model","thinking","thought_level"]
  [AFTER - fix] delegate called WITH input handle
  [AFTER - fix] thinking + thought_level aliases PRESENT
  [AFTER - fix] delegate-owned array unchanged: ["reasoning_effort","model"]
  ✅ Gateway injects thinking default → backend ACCEPTS
```

### Non-Codex gating

Non-Codex ACP agents (Claude, etc.) do NOT get aliases injected — the `isCodexAcpCommand` gate prevents advertising aliases that only the Codex-specific wrapper can translate:

```
  [GATE] non-Codex getCapabilities → ["reasoning_effort","model"]
  [GATE] No aliases injected for non-Codex (correct)
```

### Full test suite passes

```
$ pnpm test:extension acpx
 Test Files  14 passed (14)
      Tests  160 passed (160)
```

### PR surface (3 files, +94/-17)

- `extensions/acpx/src/runtime.ts` — forward handle, gate aliases to Codex ACP
- `extensions/acpx/src/runtime.test.ts` — 3 new tests for forwarding, alias injection, non-Codex gating
- `src/agents/acp-spawn.ts` — restore `resolveThinkingDefault` fallback

target.title: Agents/tool-images: memoize resize to avoid per-turn sharp decode (#64418)
target.body:
## Summary

Session history is re-sanitized on every turn via `sanitizeSessionMessagesImages`, which means `resizeImageBase64IfNeeded` is invoked for the same historical image on every message. Both the `getImageMetadata` header read and any `resizeToJpeg` call are expensive sharp decodes, so we memoize the result with a collision-safe, byte-bounded LRU cache.

Fixes #64418.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Skills / tool execution

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #64418
- Related #64514 (prior attempt, auto-closed under `too-many-prs`; this PR addresses both review concerns raised there — see below)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## What's in scope

- Add SHA-256-keyed resize-result cache in `src/agents/tool-images.ts`.
- Eviction by total cached bytes with a fixed internal 64 MiB cap.
- Focused cache regression tests in `tool-images.test.ts` plus a cache reset in `tool-images.log.test.ts`.

## Addressing #64514 review feedback

#64514 was a prior attempt that was auto-closed under the `too-many-prs` rule, not rejected on merits. Two substantive review concerns were raised there (by `@greptile-apps` and `@chatgpt-codex-connector`); both are addressed upfront here:

- **P1 (cache-key collision).** #64514 hashed only `base64.slice(0, 1000)`, which collides across JPEGs that share SOI + APP0/JFIF + DQT + DHT headers — silently substituting one image's bytes for another's in the model context. This PR hashes the full base64 payload. SHA-256 over several MB is sub-millisecond and still far cheaper than the sharp decode we skip on a cache hit.
- **P2 (unbounded memory).** #64514 used a 200-entry count-based cap, worst-case ≈ 1.3 GB RSS. This PR uses a byte-bounded LRU (64 MiB default), so total cache footprint is fixed regardless of entry size.

Credit to `@EronFan` for the original repro and the call-site integration.

## Tests

- **`keys on the full base64 payload so long shared prefixes do not collide (#64514 P1)`** — direct unit test on `computeResizeCacheKey`. Constructs two strings with a 1024-char identical leading prefix and asserts the keys differ. Mutation-verified: I temporarily patched the keyer to `hash.update(base64.slice(0, 1000))` and confirmed this test fails with `expected '213f2963...' not to be '213f2963...'`, then reverted.
- **`records separate cache entries for two distinct valid images (#64418 end-to-end)`** — wires through `sanitizeContentBlocksImages` with two different valid JPEGs to prove the key is routed through the actual cache wrapper (not just the internal helper).
- **`reuses the resize result for the same image across repeated calls`** — simulates the session-history replay, asserts `misses=1, hits=1` after two calls with the same block.
- **`keys the cache by maxBytes so different limits do not share results`**.
- **`bounds cache memory by evicting past the byte cap`** — deterministic test: sets cap to 1 byte and verifies `entryCount=0, totalBytes <= maxBytes` after three inserts.
- **`tool-images.log.test.ts`** — cache reset added to `beforeEach` so the shared PNG used across tests doesn't let a cache hit silently skip the log lines the tests are asserting on.

## Benchmark

10 turns, same 47 KB PNG (via `tsx`):

| Config | Total | Per turn | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cold (cache reset each turn) | 51.9 ms | 5.19 ms | 1× |
| Hot  (cache retained)        | 10.3 ms | 1.03 ms | **5.1×** |

`Image resized to fit limits` log fires **1× instead of 10×** — matches the duplicate-log symptom described in #64418.

## Real Behavior Proof

> **Added 2026-05-18** in response to [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/68677#issuecomment-4354745918) asking for after-fix evidence beyond the synthetic benchmark above. This section uses the actual `sanitizeContentBlocksImages` function this PR memoizes, with cache stats read back from the same `__testing.getResizeCacheStats()` hook the unit tests use.

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Per #64418, OpenClaw re-decodes the same historical image with sharp on every agent turn because `sanitizeSessionMessagesImages` re-sanitizes the whole session history each turn. Symptom: `Image resized to fit limits` log line fires once per turn instead of once per distinct image. This PR memoizes the resize result keyed by SHA-256 over the full base64 payload (collision-safe) and effective sanitizer limits, with byte-bounded LRU eviction under a fixed internal 64 MiB cap.

**Real environment tested:** Local node v22.14.0 + sharp built from `pnpm install`. Generated a real 4096x4096 PNG via sharp (228 KB) to make the resize work non-trivial. Imported the actual exports from this PR's `src/agents/tool-images.ts` (`sanitizeContentBlocksImages` + `__testing.{resetResizeCache, getResizeCacheStats}`) — no mocks, no synthetic shortcut.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
1. Rebuilt the cache on top of current `origin/main` sanitizer behavior (current HEAD `7e48708154`): preserves `readImageMetadataFromHeader` header-only no-op pass-through, `MAX_IMAGE_INPUT_PIXELS`, backend-unavailable handling, `resolveIntegerOption` normalization, and current media-core imports.
2. Removed the proposed `OPENCLAW_IMAGE_RESIZE_CACHE_MAX_BYTES` operator env knob and release-owned `CHANGELOG.md` edit; production cache retention is a fixed internal 64 MiB byte cap.
3. `pnpm test src/agents/tool-images.test.ts src/agents/tool-images.log.test.ts` → **18 passed**.
3. Wrote a focused Node driver `src/agents/.proof-image-cache.mts` that: generates a real 4096x4096 PNG with sharp, calls `sanitizeContentBlocksImages([imgBlock], "proof")` 10 times in two scenarios — (a) **cold**: `__testing.resetResizeCache()` between every call (simulates current main where the cache doesn't exist); (b) **hot**: cache retained across calls (this PR's behavior). Times each call with `perf_hooks.performance.now()` and reads back `__testing.getResizeCacheStats()` at the end.
4. `node --import tsx src/agents/.proof-image-cache.mts`.

**Evidence after fix:**

Captured terminal output (redacted of nothing — all values are deterministic synthetic content):

```text
[setup] generating realistic 4096x4096 PNG (cause sharp to do real decode work)…
[setup] generated 233666 bytes (~228 KiB)

[cold] simulating MAIN: reset cache between every turn (same image, decoded N times)
[agents/tool-images] Image resized to fit limits: 4096x4096px 228.2KB -> 4.4KB (-98.1%)
[cold turn 1] 195.65 ms
[agents/tool-images] Image resized to fit limits: 4096x4096px 228.2KB -> 4.4KB (-98.1%)
[cold turn 2] 89.37 ms
... [8 more identical "Image resized to fit limits" log lines + cold turn timings 70-90 ms each] ...
[cold turn 10] 70.94 ms
[cold] final stats: hits=0 misses=1 entryCount=1

[hot] simulating PR: cache retained across turns (same image, decoded once, cached after)
[agents/tool-images] Image resized to fit limits: 4096x4096px 228.2KB -> 4.4KB (-98.1%)
[hot turn 1] 70.82 ms
[hot turn 2] 5.92 ms
[hot turn 3] 6.45 ms
[hot turn 4] 6.47 ms
[hot turn 5] 6.15 ms
[hot turn 6] 6.94 ms
[hot turn 7] 6.23 ms
[hot turn 8] 6.67 ms
[hot turn 9] 6.10 ms
[hot turn 10] 6.30 ms
[hot] final stats: hits=9 misses=1 entryCount=1

============================================================
[summary] 10 turns, single 4096x4096 PNG
[summary] cold total: 876.31 ms (avg 87.63 ms/turn)
[summary] hot  total: 128.03 ms (avg 12.80 ms/turn)
[summary] speedup:    6.84×
[summary] hot cache:  hits=9 misses=1 (expected 9/1)

[PROOF] ✓ resize cache eliminates 9/10 sharp decodes for repeated session-history images
[PROOF] ✓ realized 6.8× speedup on session-history replay of the same image
```

**Observed result after fix:** Three independent signals from real terminal output all confirm the fix:
1. **Cache stats** (read back from `__testing.getResizeCacheStats()`, the same hook the unit tests use): hot scenario shows `hits=9 misses=1` — exactly one decode for 10 invocations of the same image.
2. **Per-turn latency**: cold turns are ~75–90 ms each (real sharp decode), hot turns 2–10 are ~6 ms each (cache hit). Speedup: **6.84×** across 10 turns.
3. **`Image resized to fit limits` log line count**: fires 10× in the cold scenario (the bug symptom), 1× in the hot scenario (the fix). This is the user-visible log-fire-count described in #64418.

**What was not tested:**
- A full openclaw chat session against a live model provider — the driver invokes the same `sanitizeContentBlocksImages` function the agent calls on every turn, but in isolation rather than through the full agent loop. The agent's call path is covered by the existing `sanitizeImageBlocks`/`sanitizeContentBlocksImages` unit tests, plus the cache hit/miss assertions added in this PR's regression suite.
- Behavior under memory pressure beyond the 1-byte eviction unit test — the byte-bounded eviction is unit-tested but not stress-tested with a real-world high-volume image stream.

## Verification

- `pnpm test src/agents/tool-images.test.ts src/agents/tool-images.log.test.ts` — 18 passed.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 pnpm check:changed` — green (typecheck, lint, import cycles, runtime-sidecar, webhook, and pairing guards).
- Linter diagnostics on touched files — 0 errors.
- Rebuilt onto current `origin/main`; no changelog entry or new runtime env/config surface remains.

## Security Impact

No new permissions, secrets/token handling, network calls, command/tool execution surface, or data-access scope changes. The cache holds already-in-memory sanitized image bytes keyed by a SHA-256 hash of those bytes plus the configured size limits; no additional data leaves the process.

## AI-assisted disclosure (per `CONTRIBUTING.md`)

- [x] Built with AI assistance (Cursor + Claude).
- [x] Testing degree: lightly tested (scoped unit + integration tests + mutation test on the collision guard; no repro on a real long session beyond the synthetic benchmark).
- [x] I understand what the code does.
- [x] Will address bot review conversations as an author.
- [ ] `codex review --base origin/main` run locally — not run, Codex CLI not available in this session.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): stop rendering misleading /compact labels on small sessions
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem**: Running \`/compact\` on a session with little or no summarizable history can render labels like \`Compacted (0 → 36) • Context 36/1.0m (0%)\` — the arrow direction is reversed, and the denominator context number is wrong.
- **Why it matters**: Users see output that implies compaction grew the context, which is confusing and erodes trust in the command. The 0%/36-token display also misrepresents actual session size.
- **What changed**: Forward \`currentTokenCount\` into the compactor (parity with the automated path), clamp the label when \`before <= after\`, and fall back to a JSONL file-size estimate when the stored totalTokens is stale.
- **What did NOT change**: No API/contract changes, no schema changes. Pure UX + one new optional forward.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] UI / DX
- [x] Integrations (messaging reply formatting — Telegram/WhatsApp/Discord all consume this line)

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

Three related issues in \`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-compact.ts\`:

1. \`handleCompactCommand\` never passed the session's observed \`currentTokenCount\` into \`compactEmbeddedPiSession\`. The underlying \`tokensBefore\` then fell through to whatever the safeguard could infer — often 0 for small sessions. The automated/preflight compaction path in \`agent-runner-memory.ts:476\` already passes \`currentTokenCount: tokenCountForCompaction\` — this brings the manual path in line.

2. The label rendering did \`Compacted (before → after)\` unconditionally, even when \`before === 0\` or \`before < after\`, producing the nonsense \`(0 → 36)\` arrow. Now only render the arrow when \`before > after\`, otherwise fall back to \`Compacted (≈N after)\` or plain \`Compacted\`.

3. The post-compaction context summary used \`resolveFreshSessionTotalTokens()\` alone. For backends/cases where \`totalTokens\` is stale — e.g. not updated per turn — this printed a tiny number next to the full context window. Added a JSONL file-size estimate (chars÷4) so the summary reflects actual on-disk session size when the stored counter is missing or lower than the file-size estimate.

## Evidence

- [x] Repro: on a Telegram session with 14 JSONL entries and stale \`totalTokens: 36\`, \`/compact\` rendered \`⚙️ Compacted (0 → 36) • Context 36/1.0m (0%)\`. After the fix it renders \`⚙️ Compaction skipped: no real conversation messages yet • Context ≈1.7k/1.0m (0%)\`.
- [x] Existing test suite in \`commands-compact.test.ts\` still passes (7/7). The tests use \`tokensBefore=999, tokensAfter=321\` which still hits the \`before > after\` branch unchanged.

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios:
  - Skipped compaction on a small Telegram session — no more \`(0 → 36)\` arrow.
  - Happy-path compaction with known token counts — arrow still renders.
  - Post-compaction context summary now reflects JSONL-derived tokens when stored count is stale.
- Edge cases checked:
  - Missing session file (stat throws) — estimator returns \`undefined\`, falls back to the stored value.
  - Empty file — estimator skips via the \`size > 0\` guard.
  - \`before === after\` — renders \`Compacted (≈N after)\` instead of \`(N → N)\`.
- What I did **not** verify: behavior when \`contextTokens\` is a very small model window (e.g. 8k). Math should still hold but I only tested with 200k/1M windows.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config/env changes? No
- Migration needed? No

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: The JSONL file-size estimate is deliberately rough (chars÷4) and can overstate tokens for transcripts heavy in tool-result JSON.
  - Mitigation: Only used as a fallback when the stored \`totalTokens\` is missing or smaller than the estimate (\`Math.max\`). If the stored number is fresh and larger, it wins. The UI label prefix \`≈\` also signals it's approximate.

target.title: ci: skip docs sync & translate-trigger workflows in forks
target.body: ## Summary - **Problem:** Two upstream-only workflows (`docs-sync-publish.yml`, `docs-translate-trigger-release.yml`) fail with `Authentication failed for 'https://github.com/openclaw/docs.git/'` on every push to `main` in any fork, because they rely on the `OPENCLAW_DOCS_SYNC_TOKEN` secret that only exists in `openclaw/openclaw`. - **Why it matters:** Creates a red ✗ on every normal fork-sync (`git fetch upstream main && git push origin main`), confuses new contributors, and spams fork Actions dashboards with irrecoverable failures. - **What changed:** Added `if: github.repository == 'openclaw/openclaw'` to the single job in each of the two workflows — the same guard pattern already used ~30 times across the repo (`ci.yml`, `codeql.yml`, `control-ui-locale-refresh.yml`). - **What did NOT change (scope boundary):** No changes to workflow logic, secrets, the publish repo, the sync script (`scripts/docs-sync-publish.mjs`), documentation, or any other workflow. Behavior in `openclaw/openclaw` is byte-for-byte identical. ## Change Type (select all) - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Refactor required for the fix - [ ] Docs - [ ] Security hardening - [x] Chore/infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [ ] Gateway / orchestration - [ ] Skills / tool execution - [ ] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [ ] Integrations - [ ] API / contracts - [ ] UI / DX - [x] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue/PR - Closes # - Related # - [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression ## Root Cause (if applicable) - **Root cause:** The two workflows were added without the fork-guard expression that the rest of the CI already uses. When the workflow runs in a fork, `${{ secrets.OPENCLAW_DOCS_SYNC_TOKEN }}` expands to an empty string, so the clone/push URL becomes `https://x-access-token:@github.com/openclaw/docs.git/` and GitHub rejects it with `Invalid username or token. Password authentication is not supported for Git operations.` - **Missing detection / guardrail:** No `if: github.repository == 'openclaw/openclaw'` on the job, even though the same repository relies on that exact check in ~30 other places to keep fork runs safe. - **Contributing context:** The workflows were likely adapted from local-only automation; the push-to-external-repo step is what makes the fork-guard a requirement rather than a nicety. ## Regression Test Plan (if applicable) - Coverage level that should have caught this: - [ ] Unit test - [ ] Seam / integration test - [ ] End-to-end test - [x] Existing coverage already sufficient - **Target test or file:** N/A — GitHub Actions `if:` expressions are evaluated by GitHub's runner and are not covered by the project's test suites. The guard syntax itself is validated by GitHub's workflow parser. - **Scenario the test should lock in:** On fork `main` push, the two docs workflows must evaluate to Skipped rather than running. - **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** A job-level `if:` is the idiomatic, zero-cost mechanism GitHub Actions provides for this; the repo already uses it extensively for the same reason. - **Existing test that already covers this (if any):** N/A. - **If no new test is added, why not:** No project-level test harness exists for workflow fork-safety; the guard is the test. Empirical verification via `workflow_dispatch` on this PR branch in a fork (see Human Verification). ## User-visible / Behavior Changes None. End users, plugins, gateway, UI, API, and config are unaffected. target.title: fix(security): add estimate-before-decode guard to base64 paths
target.body:
## Summary
- Problem: Four locations decode base64 payloads before checking size limits, risking transient OOM if a provider/tool returns an oversized payload.
- Solution: Add estimate-before-decode guards where safe, preserve existing behavior contracts where compatibility matters.
- What changed:
  - `src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.ts`: writeCliImages adds maxBytes param, estimates before Buffer.from
  - `src/image-generation/image-assets.ts`: Estimates decoded size before canonicalization to avoid transient string allocation
  - `src/agents/utils/image-resize.ts`: Removed pre-decode check to preserve resize capability for legitimate larger images
  - `src/music-generation/provider-assets.ts`: Restored original return type to maintain plugin SDK compatibility
- What did NOT change: resizeImage still attempts resize before rejecting; generatedMusicAssetFromBase64 still returns guaranteed result.

## Real behavior proof
- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Base64 decode-before-bounds defense-in-depth gap with attention to compatibility.
- **Real environment tested:** Task worktree with node --import tsx direct function invocation.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { resizeImage } from "./src/agents/utils/image-resize.ts"; import { generatedImageAssetFromBase64 } from "./src/image-generation/image-assets.ts"; import { generatedMusicAssetFromBase64 } from "./src/music-generation/provider-assets.ts"; // ... tests ...'
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  === Test 1: image-resize preserves resize capability ===
  Medium payload base64 chars: 14000
  Estimated decoded bytes: 10500
  resizeImage result for medium payload: null
  (null expected because Rastermill unavailable in test, but it tried to process)
  
  === Test 2: image-assets estimates before canonicalization ===
  Oversized payload base64 chars: 200
  Estimated decoded bytes: 150
  generatedImageAssetFromBase64 oversized result: undefined
  (undefined expected, rejected before canonicalization)
  generatedImageAssetFromBase64 normal result buffer: tiny-image
  
  === Test 3: music helper preserves SDK contract ===
  generatedMusicAssetFromBase64 return type: object
  generatedMusicAssetFromBase64 fileName: track-1.mp3
  generatedMusicAssetFromBase64 mimeType: audio/mpeg
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:**
  1. image-resize attempts processing for resizeable images instead of early rejection
  2. image-assets rejects oversized payloads before canonicalization (no transient string allocation)
  3. music helper maintains guaranteed return type for SDK compatibility
- **What was not tested:** Live Rastermill resize (requires image processor backend); only verified logic path preserves resize opportunity.

## Regression Test Plan
- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts, src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts, src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts
- Scenario locked in: Oversized base64 payload rejected before canonicalization; normal payloads decode successfully; music helper returns guaranteed result.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Tests the exact security invariant (estimate-before-decode where safe) while preserving compatibility contracts.

## Root Cause
- Root cause: Functions skipped the "estimate decoded bytes before decode" guard in some paths, and applied it incorrectly in others (blocking resize, breaking SDK contracts).
- Missing detection / guardrail: Pre-canonicalization size check in image-assets; understanding that maxBytes is an output target not an input ceiling for resizeImage; SDK compatibility requirement for music helper.
